reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-02: nothing dispatches this command. The only mentions outside the native dispatch are the dev mock (ui/src/bridge.mock.ts) and ui/src/agent/commandClassification.ts; the Lyrics panel has no cancel control and the agent command list (ui/src/agent/commands.ts) does not offer it, so there is no UI path for an e2e spec to drive. Natively it only bumps lyricGenEpoch_ so an in-flight async generation skips its landing (MoshOps.Lyrics.cpp cmdCancelLyricJob); that effect is observable only with a generation in flight, which needs the generative service. A hermetic selftest could assert ok + the JSONL record and nothing more. The Finish My Song program has been paused since 2026-08-11 (CLAUDE.md), so this is a structural hold, not a to-do: on expiry either renew, add that minimal selftest check in a native PR, or delete the command if FMS stays parked. The previous 'service-spawning by design' wording was wrong for this command (it never touches the service) and is dropped.

Re-reviewed 2026-10-02: still unquoted on every ledger surface, and a cover was attempted and blocked. The LoRA Lab is the caller (stopLabRun in ui/src/store/loraLab.ts, the lab-stop button in ui/src/ui/LoraLab.tsx). An e2e Train -> Stop spec cannot run today because the dev mock never sets `eligible` on a training source (native TrainerRegistry does), so the Lab's Train button stays disabled and no run can be started from the UI; the mock job is also 'ready' the instant it is submitted, so the spec needs Playwright's paused clock to keep Stop on screen. Cheapest cover: derive `eligible`/`blocked_reason` in the mock's training registry, then add that Train -> Stop spec to ui/e2e/lora-lab.spec.ts asserting cancel_training_job {jobId} in the command trace; this retires training_job_status in the same PR. scripts/verify-hardware/lab_train_check.py still never issues the command, and extending it needs a live SA3 + pmetal run to verify.

Re-reviewed 2026-10-02: still unquoted on every ledger surface and absent from vitest (bridge.mock.ts, ui/src/ui/TopbarTools.tsx and commandClassification.ts only). The UI path exists (the training popover's 'Import adapter' / per-job 'Import' buttons), but an e2e spec can only reach the REFUSAL: mock training jobs carry a stub adapter.lora.json artifact, which the mock rejects exactly as native does ('unsupported source extension'). The success path - validate, stage, install into $MOSH_LORA_DIR/sa3 through jobManager.installLora - needs a real .safetensors from a real run; the install itself is proven service-side by service/loras/install_test.py, the native command is not. Cheapest real cover: have scripts/verify-hardware/lab_train_check.py import the finished run's artifact by jobId and assert the adapter appears in the registry. That needs a live SA3 service and a pmetal fine-tune to verify, so it was not done in this pass.

Re-reviewed 2026-10-02: still unquoted on every ledger surface. The LoRA Lab polls it once a second while a run is live (pollLabRun in ui/src/store/loraLab.ts), but no e2e spec can start a run: the dev mock never sets `eligible` on a training source, so the Lab's Train button stays disabled (see cancel_training_job). It is also in the mock's READONLY set, so it never appears in the e2e command trace; the observable is the Lab run header moving to 'stopped'/'done', which only this read can cause. scripts/verify-hardware/lab_train_check.py still polls the service's /training/status over HTTP and never issues the command. Cheapest cover: the Train -> Stop e2e spec described under cancel_training_job, which retires both waivers together.
